text: You've just taken over as sysadmin for a mid-sized company's mixed Windows and Linux estate, with ninety days to bring the whole thing up to a real, auditable baseline before the next external review. Every chapter of this course is a piece of those ninety days, and this lesson walks through exactly how they fit together.

Week one starts with an inventory of what's actually in Active Directory — the domain structure, the OUs, who's in which security group, and which NTFS and share permissions have quietly drifted. Week two applies the fix: a CIS-based GPO baseline, firewall rules scoped correctly by profile, BitLocker with recovery keys escrowed to AD, and audit policy plus Sysmon configured so the logs actually capture what happened, not just that something did.

Week three moves to Linux: sudoers files get scoped to exactly what each role needs, PAM policies get reviewed, file permissions and ACLs get audited, and cron jobs and systemd timers get checked for excess access. Week four layers on SELinux or AppArmor enforcing mode, auditd rules watching the files an auditor cares about, SSH hardened to key-only auth, and fail2ban watching the door behind it.

From there, the ongoing work takes over: a real Patch Tuesday and apt or dnf cadence instead of patching whenever someone remembers, vulnerability scans tracked by CVE and CVSS score, and endpoint protection, EDR on Windows and a Linux-appropriate equivalent, backed by an asset inventory that actually lists every machine. None of this protects a server nobody knew existed in the first place.

By day ninety, the environment isn't just patched, it's documented and auditable, built so the next review doesn't turn into the same case study this chapter just walked through. That's the full course — from what a domain controller does to hardening, patching, and defending both operating systems you'll actually work on. Course complete. Next up in this path: Network Security, Endpoint Protection & Threat Detection.
